title: The Demographic Siege
lede: Since the 1909 tract that called Hindus “a dying race”, Hindu nationalists have warned that India's Muslim share is growing. Critics called this paranoia. Elst checks the claim against the census from 1881 to 1991 and examines migration from Bangladesh, Muslim and Hindu fertility, and Islamic teaching on birth control. His conclusion is that the trend is real, though slower than the alarmists said. He rejects “panicky solutions” such as a Hindu birth race and argues for persuasion and reconversion instead.

note: Demographic projections are sensitive and often misused. Since this book, the 2011 census recorded Muslims at 14.2% of India's population. National surveys show fertility falling among all religious groups, fastest among Muslims, which narrows the gap Elst projected forward. This page reports his figures and argument as his, with the later census added for context.

sections.title: Elst's verdict and his prescription
items: On the trend, the Hindu nationalists, in his view. He projects a Muslim majority in the subcontinent this century and Muslim-majority pockets in India sooner.
He rejects a Hindu “demographic counter-offensive” and any coercive scheme.
Dayananda's approach: persuade Muslims to reconsider Islam, and welcome them back.
